one_liner: Senior manager (GS-15) leading FEMA's Financial Policy Branch, directing staff who write financial and travel policy and advising CFO leadership in the DC area.
fit_summary: This role requires one full year of GS-14-equivalent experience directing financial management systems policy, advising senior leaders on financial policy or legislation, and analyzing financial policies. Daniel's policy knowledge and IEM emergency-management consulting are relevant to FEMA's mission, but nothing on file shows senior financial policy or supervisory experience at that level. Apply only if your IEM work truly involved leading financial policy, grants or cost-compliance work for clients.
eligibility: Open to the public and transitioning feds. As a U.S. citizen with no federal service, Daniel can apply, and the time-in-grade rule applies only to current federal employees.

You need one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-14 covering all three areas: staff direction on financial management information systems policy, advising senior leadership on financial policies or legislation, and analyzing and communicating financial policies.
No education substitution is allowed. Experience alone must qualify you.
You must pass a Public Trust High-Risk background investigation with a credit check, obtain a Government credit card, and be registered with Selective Service if required.
You must be able to deploy with little or no notice anywhere in the U.S. and its territories for extended periods.
keywords: draft new policies, standards, and guidance
strategy: Be honest when you check the specialized experience against all three required areas. Proceed only if IEM work like grant cost-reimbursement, FEMA Public Assistance financial compliance or budget policy for government clients fills a full year at senior scope.

If you apply, write the IEM entry in your own words with MM/DD/YY dates, hours per week, job title, and specific financial-policy and leadership duties. Do not copy the announcement text, and keep the resume to two pages.
Frame any work interpreting federal regulations (for example 2 CFR 200, Stafford Act, or FEMA cost guidance) for clients as policy research and advising senior officials.
Preview the USA Hire questionnaire and the Applicant Resource Center before applying, and plan an uninterrupted block to take the assessment.

Mark the window of 10/30 to 11/09/2026 and submit early. Separately, target FEMA, DHS, or Virginia VDEM positions at GS-9 to GS-12 or in policy, external affairs, or legislative roles that better match your background.
resume_bullets: Advised [client agency/senior official title] on [federal financial or grant regulation], interpreting requirements and drafting [number] guidance documents adopted by [organization].
Led a team of [number] staff to [develop/review] [financial or cost-compliance policy/process], setting priorities and allocating resources across [number] concurrent projects.
Analyzed [financial policy/legislation] and briefed [audience] through [memos/presentations], resulting in [verifiable outcome].
interview_questions: Describe a time you researched new legislation or regulations and turned them into organizational financial policy.
How have you advised senior leaders on a financial policy decision they disagreed with?
How do you assign, monitor, and evaluate the work of a policy team under tight deadlines?
How would you handle being deployed to a disaster for weeks on short notice while still running your branch?
watch_outs: The GS-15 specialized experience in financial management is the major barrier, and a resume without clear senior financial-policy leadership will be rated not qualified.
This is a Schedule Policy/Career excepted-service job: at-will, with no MSPB appeal rights for adverse actions.
There is no telework, plus a credit-check background investigation and possible extended, austere deployments.
The application window is short, only about 10 days.
